messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT ALERT — Control plane elevated 5xx rate
incident-bot: Metric: control-plane /requests 5xx rate = 11.9% over 5m (baseline 0.3%)
incident-bot: Top dependent failures: billing-service (504s), config-service (timeouts)
incident-bot: Pager escalated to #incidents oncall -> oncall-anna
oncall-anna: seeing it, pulling up dashboards. 504s seem concentrated on /billing/lookup
oncall-anna: initial customer impact: API calls involving payment status are failing intermittently, some customers see errors on checkout flows
sre-marc: joining — any obvious deploys in last 30m?
eng-ops-alejandra: there was a canary of config-rollout ~25m ago that changed billing hook timeout from 2s -> 8s
infra-jay: scaling up billing replica set now
infra-jay: run: kubectl -n billing scale deploy/billing-api --replicas=6
oncall-anna: thanks, infra-jay. can we also put a soft circuit-break on control-plane to avoid cascading errors?
sre-marc: agree. recommend setting fallback to cached-billing for 60s and open circuit at 30% 5xx
oncall-anna: applying fallback switch via feature-flag manager, patching to return cached responses for billing lookups
oncall-anna: patch command:
```
curl -X POST https://flags.internal/api/toggle -d '{"flag":"billing.lookup.use_cache","value":true}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx'
```
eng-ops-alejandra: rolling back the timeout change on config-service; opening a rollback PR now
eng-ops-alejandra: PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/config/rollbacks/234
sre-marc: adding rate-limit on upstream calls to billing from control-plane
sre-marc: nginx snippet applied on control-plane:
```
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=b_billing:10m rate=20r/s;
location /billing/ {
  limit_req zone=b_billing burst=40 nodelay;
}
```
oncall-anna: monitoring: 5xx dropped from 11.9% -> 6.2% after scaling + cache fallback (2m)
cust-ops-sam: heads-up for CS: customers might see ~30min of partial failures; prepare status page draft — I’ll start it
cust-ops-sam: status page (draft): "We are investigating elevated errors affecting billing lookups. Some customers may see intermittent failures. Working on mitigation."
infra-jay: still seeing increased latency on billing DB connections, adding one more read-replica
infra-jay: aws rds add-read-replica --db billing-primary --class db.r5.large
eng-ops-alejandra: config rollback merged and hotpatch deployed to config-service (v2.3.1-hotfix)
oncall-anna: after config rollback + cache fallback + scaling: 5xx = 1.8% over 5m, timeouts mostly gone
sre-marc: leaving a follow-up action item: instrument billing call path for slow queries (trace spans missing), create alert for DB connection saturations
sre-marc: ticket created: INT-4521
oncall-anna: handing incident to cust-ops-sam for comms and to infra-jay for postmortem work — I'm off in 30m, taking handoff to night oncall
cust-ops-sam: acknowledged — will update status page and coordinate customer comms
infra-jay: acknowledged — will keep infra ownership, will collect DB/OS metrics and timeline
eng-ops-alejandra: will do a deeper query-profile analysis and follow-up PR to tune billing SQL and add connection pooling improvements
incident-bot: NOTE: Incident severity set -> SEV2. Pages: 3, Duration so far: ~22m
cust-ops-sam: closing notes: minimal ongoing impact, continue monitoring. If error rate stays <2% for next 20m we can move to retrospective
oncall-anna: thanks team. added retrospective notes and mitigation timeline to INT-4521
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations in place; monitoring watches set.
